nodes.question: What sources are referenced in the context of governance of inter-organizational networks?
nodes.answer: The sources referenced include works by Glicker (2020), Glicker and Nemeth (2012), Klijn et al. (2010), and Provan and Kenis (2008).

In such a perspec- tive, MSIs are understood as an arena where heterogeneousactors meet. However, a common understanding about the governance of MSIs has not yet been established within interdisciplinary discourse (Bryson et al. 2015 ; de Bakker et al. 2019 ; Gazley 2017 ; Getha-Taylor et al. 2019 ; GI ckler 2020 ; van Tulder et al. 2016 ). The central question of this paper is therefore: how can the governance of an MSI inglobal economic relations be captured empirically to explain (un)achieved outcomes of the collaboration?Environmental Management (2025) 75:490 504 491 To answer this question, we propose a theoretical fra- mework for capturing and analyzing the governance of MSIs. We build this on work on the governance of inter- organizational (corporate) networks (GI ckler 2020 ; GI ckler and N meth 2012 ; Klijn et al. 2010 ; Provan and Kenis 2008 ). We understand the concept of networks from a relational perspective, which contributes to a better under- standing of social processes on the one hand and social relations on the other (Grabher 2006 ).

nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What approach was used to explore the responses of the network attributes along the LUD and SPEI gradients?
nodes.answer: The responses of the network attributes were explored using network analysis and a moving-window approach.
nodes.paragraph: To gain insights into these responses, we quantified land use and climate change using land-use dynamics (LUD) and the standardized precipitation evapotranspiration index (SPEI), respectively. Subsequently, an SES network was constructed by incorporating six distinct socio-ecological factors. Furthermore, the responses of the network attributes along the LUD and SPEI gradients were explored using network analysis and a moving-window approach. The aims of this study were to (1) construct a network among SES components in the YRB, (2) explore the effects of land-use and climate change on SES network coupling relationships, and (3) identify their thresholds to guide ecological zoning management. Materials and methods Study areas The YRB (90 33 122 25 E, 24 30 35 45 N) covers 1.8 million km2 across 11 provinces, cities, and autonomous regions (Fig. 1). The topography of the YRB varies, with the ground gradually rising from southeast to northwest. With the influence of monsoon circulation, the YRB experiences a subtropical climate characterized by an annual precipitation range of 1000 to 1400 mm and an average annual temperature fluctuating between 12 and 18 C40.
